cues.en: looked like this. You have a system that takes in a query received by a front end web server. The index is actually divided into a bunch of partitions by document. So some of each of these partitions has some of the documents across the whole system.

cues.zh: 你向索引服务系统中的每个分区发送请求。

cues.zh: 所以这样一个系统的设计基本原则是，

cues.zh: 然后把一堆这样的配对返回给你。

cues.en: And the cost of the index serving portion of the system is essentially order number of queries times the number of documents in the index that you're searching.
cues.zh: 系统里索引服务部分的成本，基本上就是查询数量乘以你要搜索的索引中的文档数量。

cues.en: On the doc server side,
cues.zh: 在文档服务器这边，

cues.en: the
cues.zh: 这里的

cues.en: that they would show as opposed to just showing the first 30 words of the document or something. That actually is a really important innovation,
cues.zh: 也就是要展示的摘要，而不是只显示文档前 30 个词之类的内容。这其实是一项非常重要的创新，

cues.en: but it does mean that
cues.zh: 但这确实意味着

cues.en: the snippet is query dependent, so you can't sort of precompute what are the snippets you want to show for every document. You have to do it for every doc ID, document cross query pair.
cues.zh: 摘要片段依赖查询，所以你不能预先算好每个文档要展示什么摘要片段。你得对每个文档 ID、每个文档与查询的组合分别来做。

cues.zh: 其实基本上就是查询的数量级。因为每个查询，你无非是返回 10 条或 20 条左右的结果。所以

cues.en: And so that will mean you'll typically get fewer cache hits than, data center in The US where you see more English queries and fewer other language queries.
cues.zh: 所以这通常意味着，你的缓存命中会比美国的数据中心少，因为那里英语查询更多，其他语言查询更少。

cues.en: Yeah. How much you personalize the search results and how that affects what you can cache.

cues.en: So the main benefits of the caching system are obviously performance because a few machines dedicated to caching,
cues.zh: 所以缓存系统的主要好处显然就是性能，因为少数几台专门做缓存的机器，

cues.en: maintaining a cache on disk do
cues.zh: 在磁盘上维护缓存，就能完成

cues.en: the work that hundreds or thousands of machines in your back end systems are actually trying to do. So a few machines do 50% of your work, then the other thousand do the other 50%.
cues.zh: 后端系统里成百上千台机器实际要做的工作。所以几台机器承担你 50% 的工作，然后另外上千台做另外 50%。

cues.en: You also get much lower query latency. So if you get cache hits, you just basically have to do one disk seek to read the data in the cache, and you return to the users. You don't have to do any of this distributed,
cues.zh: 你还能获得低得多的查询延迟。所以如果命中缓存，基本上只需一次磁盘寻址读出缓存里的数据，然后返回给用户。你不用做任何分布式，

cues.en: distribution
cues.zh: 分发

cues.en: of RPCs to to shards and so on. And also the queries that hit in the cache tend to be both popular because, obviously, they hit in the cache, someone else has already issued this query, and expensive.
cues.zh: 的 RPC 到各个分片等等。而且命中缓存的查询往往既热门——因为显然它们命中了缓存，说明已经有别人发过这个查询——又昂贵。

cues.en: You know, they tend to be shorter queries, single word queries that tend to have a lot of results. And you end up having,
cues.zh: 你知道，这类查询通常比较短，甚至是单个词的查询，但往往会有大量结果。最终你会遇到，

cues.en: lots of documents that get retrieved for these queries and lots of documents to score.
cues.zh: 这些查询会检索出大量文档，也有大量文档需要打分。

cues.en: One of the things to be aware of is that there's a big latency spike
cues.zh: 需要注意的一点是，刷新缓存或更新索引时，会出现明显的延迟峰值，

cues.zh: 以及容量的大幅下降。所以我们也必须谨慎安排

cues.zh: 上线新索引的时机，

cues.zh: 那么，

cues.zh: 我不打算过多讲我们的索引系统，

The initial versions didn't really even have checkpointing, so you just kind of try to take a whole bunch of the raw documents on disk,
cues.zh: 除非，也许稍后讲到它后期版本时会提一点。但在 1988 年、98 年和 99 年，它基本上就是个简单的批量索引系统。它没有……最初的版本甚至没有检查点机制，所以你就是试着把磁盘上一大堆原始文档全部拿过来，

cues.en: take all the words from them, sort them, and invert them. And,
cues.zh: 从中取出所有单词，排序，然后做倒排。而且，

cues.zh: 你基本上

cues.en: We didn't actually have checks summing of the raw data, and the machines we bought at that time, consumer class machines typically didn't have... Not only didn't they have ECC, they didn't even have parity
cues.zh: 我们其实没有对原始数据做校验和，而且当时买的机器，消费级机器通常也没有……不仅没有 ECC，甚至连奇偶校验都没有

cues.zh: 在它们的内存里。

cues.zh: 所以，在没有奇偶校验的情况下给 1TB 数据排序，挺让人崩溃的一点是：最后它会变得大体有序。

cues.zh: 所以这对归并排序尤其糟糕，因为你翻转一个比特，然后突然间，你就会忽略掉那个特定

cues.en: input file you're merging.
cues.zh: 你正在合并的输入文件下游的所有数据。

cues.zh: 我的一位同事把这比作……用对抗性内存编程。

cues.zh: 于是我们开发了——我们早期开发的模块之一是一个文件抽象，用于……专为小记录设计，会附加小校验和，并且能够重新同步

cues.zh: 采用重新同步模式

cues.en: when it detected corruption.

cues.zh: 这套东西今天仍被用于各种场景，

cues.en: and it's pretty useful.
cues.zh: 而且相当有用。

cues.zh: 所以随着我们变得更成熟，我们逐渐

cues.zh: 所以，

cues.zh: 其中一个

cues.zh: 大单。于是我们在2000年7月与Yahoo签了协议，为他们提供搜索服务，基本上我们的流量一夜之间就翻倍了

cues.zh: 我们在索引服务系统的性能上做了大量工作。我们尽可能快地部署更多机器，但它，

cues.en: was still pretty challenging, and you couldn't really deploy... We couldn't operationally deploy them as fast as we could. So we basically needed to come up with lots of software improvements over that period,
cues.zh: 仍然相当有挑战性，而且你没法真正部署……我们没法按想要的速度在运维上部署它们。所以那段时间我们基本上得想出大量软件改进，

cues.en: as we kind of... So we kind of roll out a new index, then we work on software improvements for a while,
cues.zh: 因为我们有点……我们先上线一个新索引，然后花一段时间做软件改进，

cues.zh: 再上线新索引，搭配一些新的 cert……新的服务器软件，希望性能更高

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: over this period, this is kind of the way things went. We we wanted to increase our index size because we believe that index size was a very important way of increasing search quality. Basically,
cues.zh: 这段时间，情况大概就是这样发展的。我们想扩大索引规模，因为我们认为索引规模是提升搜索质量的一个非常重要的方式。基本上，

cues.en: you wanna be the place where if you do a search and there's a page on the web, you find that page. And in order to do that, you have to have a very large index. So we're constantly
cues.zh: 你想成为这样一个地方：用户搜索时，只要网上有那个页面，就能找到它。而要做到这一点，就必须有非常大的索引。所以我们一直在

cues.en: increasing the size of the index.
cues.zh: 不断扩大索引规模。

cues.en: When you increase the size of the index, you have to keep partitioning it more finely in order to keep response times within a reasonable rate. If you tried to have, like, one or two index partitions, your latency would be too high. So essentially, as you're increasing the index size, you're adding more and more index partitions. And as traffic is growing, you're adding more and more replicas.
cues.zh: 当你增大索引规模时，必须把它切分得越来越细，才能让响应时间保持在合理水平。如果只设一两个索引分区，延迟就会太高。所以本质上，随着索引规模增长，你会不断增加索引分区；而随着流量增长，你会不断增加副本。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: there goes more shards,
cues.zh: 又多了更多分片，

cues.en: bunch more shards, more replicas,
cues.zh: 一大堆分片，更多副本，

cues.en: more shards.
cues.zh: 更多分片。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: a rather large problem with sharding the index this way
cues.zh: 这样对索引做分片，有一个相当大的问题

cues.en: is that you end up,
cues.zh: 就是最终你会

cues.en: basically on every
cues.zh: 基本上在每一个

cues.en: index shard doing a seek for every term in the query. And so disk seeks are not the most,
cues.zh: 索引分片上，都要为查询中的每个词做一次寻道。而磁盘寻道并不是最、

cues.en: highly performant operations one can do.
cues.zh: 高性能的操作。

cues.en: And so you end up basically
cues.zh: 所以最终你基本上

cues.en: being very disk seek limited and not really utilizing all the disk bandwidth you you have there. Now there are lot of tricks you can do. You can build,
cues.zh: 会严重受限于磁盘寻道，并不能真正利用好手头的全部磁盘带宽。这里有很多技巧可用。你可以构建，

cues.zh: 其他类型的磁盘辅助数据结构，通过对查询中经常出现的词预先求交，让你每次寻道能获得更多信息。

cues.en: You can try to
cues.zh: 你可以试着

cues.en: compress the index data so you have to read less data from disk, which will help you because then,
cues.zh: 压缩索引数据，这样从磁盘读取的数据就更少，这会有帮助，因为这样一来，

cues.en: in the time you're not seeking, you have to read less stuff.
cues.zh: 在不用寻道的时间里，你需要读取的数据就更少。

cues.en: But essentially, it becomes
cues.zh: 但本质上，这会变得

cues.en: more and more problematic.
cues.zh: 越来越成问题。

cues.en: Now one issue is, as you try to work on index compression
cues.zh: 现在有个问题是，当你尝试做索引压缩时

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: you add more and more machines,
cues.zh: 你增加越来越多的机器，

cues.en: you eventually realize that, you
cues.zh: 你最终会意识到，你

cues.en: know,
cues.zh: 知道，

cues.en: if I looked at all these machines we're using to serve this index,
cues.zh: 如果看看我们用来服务这个索引的所有这些机器，

cues.en: I could actually hold one copy of the index in memory across all these machines.
cues.zh: 我其实可以把一份索引副本放在所有这些机器的内存里。

cues.en: So in 2001, that's actually what we did is we had a completely in memory index system, and we've had that pretty much ever since,
cues.zh: 所以在2001年，我们实际做的就是一套完全基于内存的索引系统，而且基本上从那以后一直如此，

cues.en: for all of our, index servers.
cues.zh: 用于我们所有的索引服务器。

cues.en: So this was basically the design we came up with.
cues.zh: 这基本上就是我们当时想出的设计。

cues.en: And there's another layer of distribution in there, what we call balancers, that we're sending the front end web server to talks to each balancer in a shard. The balancer then talks to each machine in the shard because there's now only one replica of any given, piece of index data. And so it has to talk to all these machines within the shard
cues.zh: 其中还有另一层分布式结构，我们称之为 balancer；前端 Web 服务器会与某个分片中的每个 balancer 通信。然后 balancer 与该分片中的每台机器通信，因为现在任意一份索引数据都只有一个副本。因此它必须与分片内的所有这些机器通信

cues.en: and gets results. The balancer kind of combines them and then sends them back up to the web server.
cues.zh: 并获取结果。balancer 会把这些结果合并起来，然后回传给 Web 服务器。

cues.en: We still have cache servers and dock servers. Those work pretty much the same way.
cues.zh: 我们还有缓存服务器和 dock 服务器。它们的工作方式基本一样。

cues.en: Now there are a lot of really good things about this.
cues.zh: 这样做有很多好处。

cues.en: First, you get a really big increase in throughput because you're no longer doing disk seeks. You're just reading from in memory data structures.
cues.zh: 首先，吞吐量会大幅提升，因为不再做磁盘寻道，只是从内存数据结构里读取。

cues.en: And you also get a very big decrease in query latency
cues.zh: 查询延迟也会大幅降低

cues.en: because
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: you're not waiting for mechanical disks and especially at the tail. So
cues.zh: 你不用再等机械磁盘，尤其是在尾部。所以

cues.en: really expensive queries in a disk based indexing system.
cues.zh: 基于磁盘的索引系统里真正昂贵的查询。

cues.zh: 这算是我们的典型例子，让我们头疼不已。

cues.zh: 我们当时在翻查询日志，想找出哪些查询特别昂贵，而这一条，

cues.zh: 比我们查看的查询样本中其余查询高出好几个数量级。就是 Circle of life 这个短语。

cues.zh: 所以，

cues.zh: 而那就是

cues.zh: 检索系统里可能遇到的最糟情况，因为你本质上是在流式遍历，

cues.en: all this data for circle and for of and for life, looking for one rare document that that has them next to each other in in a phrase.
cues.zh: 为 circle、of 和 life 流过所有这些数据，寻找一篇罕见的文档，其中它们以短语形式紧挨在一起。

cues.en: I think we did,
cues.zh: 我想我们确实做了，

cues.en: 30 gigabytes of IO for this query.
cues.zh: 这个查询产生了 30 GB 的 IO。

cues.en: And in the memory system, it's it's very fast because the seeks don't really cost you much. You just kind
cues.zh: 而在内存系统中，它非常快，因为寻址并不会带来多少开销。你只需要

cues.zh: 在内存中的倒排列表里移到另一个位置，就可以继续了。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: when you have the index system in memory, there are two main issues that really bite you as you're first starting to deploy such a system. One is variance.
cues.zh: 当索引系统放在内存中时，刚开始部署这类系统，有两个主要问题会真正坑到你。一个是波动性。

cues.en: So the query is now gonna touch thousands of machines, not just dozens.
cues.zh: 所以现在一个查询会触达数千台机器，而不只是几十台。

cues.zh: 因此，像随机化的 cron 任务这类东西就会给你带来麻烦。

cues.zh: 而原因是，

cues.en: And it would be good to randomize those across different machines so that not all the machines were actually
cues.zh: 把这些任务在不同机器上随机化会更好，这样就不会所有机器都在

cues.en: running those cron jobs at five minute intervals, but were kind of spaced out a bit.
cues.zh: 每五分钟同时运行那些 cron 任务，而是稍微错开一些。

cues.en: And it turns out for an in memory index, this is the
cues.zh: 而事实证明，对于内存索引来说，这

cues.en: entirely
cues.zh: 完全

cues.en: opposite thing of what you actually want.
cues.zh: 是你实际想要的效果的反面。

cues.en: Because at any given point, if you've randomized things, at least one machine is doing this con job of activity, and so has less CPU or is, like, busy churning its disk or something like that,
cues.zh: 因为在任何时刻，如果你做了随机化，至少有一台机器在执行这个任务，因此 CPU 更少，或者像在忙着折腾磁盘之类的，

cues.en: sending stuff over its network.

cues.zh: 嗯。用 MapReduce 计算 PageRank 时，你们会做哪些特别的处理？有很多优化，但……对 PageRank 来说，很多优化并不在 MapReduce 上。而且我没怎么看到 Google 具体说明你们到底是怎么做的。

cues.en: Yeah. I mean, there's there's a lot of things we don't,
cues.zh: 是啊，我是说，有很多东西我们并不会，

cues.en: necessarily publish very detailed papers on.
cues.zh: 专门发表非常详细的论文。

cues.en: You know, it is possible to compute,
cues.zh: 你知道，是能计算的，

cues.en: page rank with MapReduce. It's just an iterative process. So in each iteration, you essentially,
cues.zh: 用 MapReduce 来计算 PageRank。它只是一个迭代过程。所以在每次迭代中，你本质上，

cues.en: you know, read through the link graph, flow
cues.zh: 你知道，遍历链接图，传递

cues.en: the weights for that iteration,
cues.zh: 该次迭代的权重，

cues.en: and then generate the outputs.
cues.zh: 然后生成输出。

cues.en: It's not necessarily the best tool to use for that particular task.
cues.zh: 对于那项特定任务来说，它未必是最合适的工具。

cues.en: So you can build a more specialized system. And if computing page rank very fast is very important to you, that you then you might not use MapReduce.
cues.zh: 所以你可以构建一个更专用的系统。而如果快速计算 PageRank 对你非常重要，那你可能就不会用 MapReduce。

cues.en: I think MapReduce is pretty effective where the model fits really well, or you're trying to get something quick and dirty running
cues.zh: 我觉得 MapReduce 在模型非常契合的场景下相当有效，或者当你只想快速弄出一个能跑起来的东西时

cues.en: you don't want to worry about optimizing the heck out of it. So once you have a system that, you know, for PageRank, need a thousand nodes or something to compute,
cues.zh: 你不想操心把它优化到极致。所以一旦你有个系统，比如做 PageRank 需要上千个节点才能算出来，

cues.en: then it makes sense to focus a little more optimization effort and maybe build something more customized.
cues.zh: 那多花点精力做优化、也许构建更定制化的东西，就说得通了。

cues.en: Yeah. Do you have any patterns,
cues.zh: 是的。你们有没有一些模式，

cues.en: that follow a map reduce, reduce, reduce chain kind of thing?
cues.zh: 会遵循 map reduce、reduce、reduce 链这类结构？

cues.en: So the question is, we have map reduce, reduce, reduce chains?
cues.zh: 所以问题是，我们会有 map reduce、reduce、reduce 链吗？

cues.en: Yeah. We would tend to implement that as a sequence of map reduces
cues.zh: 是的。我们倾向于把它实现成一系列 map reduce，

cues.en: and where the map task essentially just out... The subsequent map task just generate output for the reduced tasks.
cues.zh: 其中 map 任务本质上只是输出……后续的 map 任务只是为 reduce 任务生成输出。

cues.en: But a pretty common pattern is to have a whole chain sequence of map reduces
cues.zh: 但一个很常见的模式是拥有一整条 map reduce 链序列，

cues.en: that each do some part of a larger algorithm
cues.zh: 其中每一步分别完成更大算法的一部分，

cues.en: in a sequence of steps.
cues.zh: 并按一系列步骤推进。

cues.en: What? You do write out and then read this as a separate thing.
cues.zh: 什么？你确实会先写出去，再把它当作单独的东西读回来。

cues.en: Sometimes you might write out to a cheaper
cues.zh: 有时你可能会写到更便宜的

cues.en: storage system, for example, if it's intermediate data, and we know we could restart the whole computation from scratch if we want.
cues.zh: 存储系统里，比如中间数据，而且我们知道需要的话，可以从头重新开始整个计算。

cues.en: Yeah. Is this something about Google Instant and what the impact of infrastructure is? Sure.
cues.zh: 对。这是不是和 Google Instant 以及基础设施的影响有关？当然。

cues.en: So Google Instant
cues.zh: 所以 Google Instant

cues.en: is basically a system that is in the background,
cues.zh: 基本上是一个在后台运行的系统，

cues.en: predicting
cues.zh: 预测

cues.en: what,
cues.zh: 什么，

cues.en: query you're actually trying to issue when you type a few characters of it. And then we'll actually prefetch the results for that.
cues.zh: 当你只输入其中几个字符时，你实际想发出的查询。然后我们会真正预取对应的结果。

cues.en: So from a, you know, a web search standpoint,
cues.zh: 所以，从网页搜索的角度来看，

cues.en: it's essentially just getting certain kinds of requests. One of the things we do is,
cues.zh: 本质上就是接收某些类型的请求。我们做的一件事是，

cues.en: when I mentioned making your system resilient to overload,
cues.zh: 当我提到让系统能承受过载时，

cues.en: those requests come tagged with a bit that says there are predictive prefetch, not something user actually pressed, enter on. And so if we get overloaded, we can drop those requests.
cues.zh: 那些请求会带有一个标记位，表明它们是预测性预取，而不是用户真的按了回车。所以如果系统过载，我们就可以丢弃这些请求。

cues.en: And other than that, it's basically just capacity.
cues.zh: 除此之外，基本上就是容量问题。

cues.en: You know, you just need more machines to do it because you're you're doing that. Turns out the predictive stuff,
cues.zh: 你知道，你只需要更多机器来做这件事，因为你就是在做这个。结果发现，预测类的东西

cues.en: does cache reasonably well
cues.zh: 缓存效果还不错

cues.en: because you're essentially predicting queries that users have issued in the past. But,
cues.zh: 因为你本质上是在预测用户过去发出的查询。但是，

cues.en: you know, it's mostly just a
cues.zh: 你知道，这主要只是一个

cues.en: resource issue, not fundamental changes in the underlying infrastructure.
cues.zh: 资源问题，而不是底层基础设施的根本性变化。

cues.en: K. One last one? Yes. One. Okay. One last question. What is your experience
cues.zh: 好。最后一个？是的。一个。好的。最后一个问题。你在

cues.en: on using distributed transactions within a
cues.zh: 单个数据中心内使用分布式事务

cues.en: single data center?
cues.zh: 有什么经验？

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: the question is, what is our experience with using distributed transactions?
cues.zh: 问题在于，我们在使用分布式事务方面有什么经验？

cues.en: So we don't have a huge amount of experience with that. A lot of the infrastructure we've built in the past has kind of avoided implementing distributed transactions.
cues.zh: 我们在这方面的经验并不多。过去我们构建的很多基础设施，都或多或少地避免了实现分布式事务。

cues.en: For example, Bigtable has single row transactions but not distributed transactions.
cues.zh: 比如，Bigtable 有单行事务，但没有分布式事务。

cues.en: In retrospect, I think that was a mistake.
cues.zh: 回过头看，我认为那是个错误。

cues.en: We probably should have added them in because what ended up happening is a lot of people did want distributed transactions,
cues.zh: 我们当初大概就应该把分布式事务加进去，因为后来的实际情况是，很多人都确实想要分布式事务，

cues.en: and so they hand rolled their own protocols,
cues.zh: 于是他们就自己动手实现协议，

cues.en: sometimes incorrectly.
cues.zh: 有时还实现错了。

cues.en: And it would have been better to build it into the infrastructure.
cues.zh: 更好的做法是把它直接构建到基础设施里。

cues.en: So in Spanner, for example, we do have distributed transactions.
cues.zh: 比如在 Spanner 里，我们确实有分布式事务。

cues.en: We don't have a lot of experience with it yet.
cues.zh: 我们对它还没有太多经验。

cues.en: There are actually places in the Bigtable implementation where it would have been useful because we also hand rolled our own protocols for a couple of the the subtle features in there, and it would have been better just to have that available to everyone. K?
cues.zh: 其实在 Bigtable 的实现里有些地方本来会用得上，因为其中几个细微特性我们也是自己手写协议的，要是能直接让所有人都用上就好了。对吧？

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。
